hook.line: Google is no longer the only one cracking down on spammy GEO tactics.
hook.visual: Handheld walking selfie outdoors, man in glasses; orange label 'Claude's new rules target GEO spam' at top, white captions with an orange word highlight below.

beats.what: News opener while walking, orange headline label pinned at the top
Cut to a screenshot of a Lily Ray post on the policy change, his face in a small inset below
Back to walking selfie: promises what it is, why people do it, how to grow safely
Explains how GEO works: AI searches, cites pages, cited pages recommending you win
Names what is being targeted: networks of fake third-party pages recommending a client
Zoom punch on 'you don't want to make the internet a worse place'
The safe method: give AI brand context plus a few minutes of your own input per piece
Self-reference: a video like this one is his favorite input, Claude drafts and posts from it
Closing aside about walking his dog anyway, ends abruptly

why_it_works: Ties a fresh policy update to a named industry voice and shows her post at 7 s, so the news feels verified
Walking selfie with a changing background gives constant motion without edits across 170 s
Self-referential payoff (this very video becomes his content) makes the method tangible
weaknesses: 170 s with a longest shot of 42.6 s; the GEO explainer middle is slow for a news hook
No CTA; the video stops on a throwaway line
After the opening screenshot there is no visual for the method he describes
for_robert: Pin an orange headline label and cut to the source post within 7 s for news reels; Fred could hold the screenshot. Avoid the long middle with no visuals and end on a clear ask.
